beginner.summary: For Python developers who have made basic LLM API calls and now need to build the tools that agents use. Covers what an agent tool is from the operator's side, writing tool specifications, descriptions and result formats that models use correctly, choosing tool granularity, actionable errors, a tool registry and dispatcher with limits, serving tools with FastMCP and annotating them, debugging with MCP Inspector, provider-hosted tools, running untrusted code in locked-down containers, Playwright browser tools, side-effect classification, human confirmation, scoped credentials, first prompt-injection experiments, audit logs and tool tests, ending with a safe helpdesk toolset capstone.
prerequisites: Writes Python 3 code with functions, type hints, virtual environments and pip or uv
Has sent at least one request to an LLM API such as the Anthropic Messages API or the OpenAI Responses API and read the JSON response
Has a laptop with rights to install Docker Engine or Docker Desktop, Node.js LTS and Python 3.12, plus API keys for Anthropic or OpenAI
outcomes: Write tool specifications, descriptions and result formats that a model selects and uses correctly, and measure the effect of changes on labelled requests
Serve annotated tools with FastMCP over stdio and debug them with MCP Inspector and host logs
Run model-written code and browser actions inside isolated environments with network, memory, process and time limits
Classify tools by side effect, gate write actions behind human confirmation, scope credentials and record every call in redacted audit logs

intermediate.summary: For engineers who have built and tested a small toolset and now run agents with many tools, real credentials and real side effects. Covers the context cost of large catalogs, tool search with deferred loading, routing to toolsets and sub-agents, code-orchestrated tool calls, comparing code execution sandboxes, jailed filesystem and shell tools, computer-use tools, writing MCP clients, remote servers over Streamable HTTP, structured output and resource links, long-running tools, OAuth scopes per tool, least-privilege identities with short-lived credentials, idempotency, plan-then-apply tools, durable approval workflows, OpenTelemetry tool tracing, containing injection from tool results, and contract tests, ending with a multi-server toolkit capstone.
prerequisites: Completed the Tool Calling beginner level or has shipped an MCP server or agent toolset with tests, annotations and confirmation for writes
Comfortable with async Python, HTTP APIs, Docker, PostgreSQL and reading JSON Web Tokens
Has a Linux machine or VM where gVisor can be installed, plus access to Keycloak or another OAuth 2.1 authorization server and an OpenTelemetry backend such as Jaeger
outcomes: Keep large tool catalogs usable with token measurement, tool search, routing and code-orchestrated calls
Choose and operate execution runtimes for code, files, shells, browsers and desktops with measured isolation
Build MCP clients and remote servers with structured output, progress, cancellation and OAuth scopes mapped to tools
Make agent actions safe to retry and review with idempotency keys, plan-then-apply tools, durable approvals, tracing and injection containment

advanced.summary: For platform, security and staff engineers who run tools for many agents, teams or tenants. Covers tool platform architecture with a gateway, registry, policy engine and runtime pools, policy as code with Open Policy Agent, information-flow control and taint tracking, adversarial testing with AgentDojo and custom suites, tool poisoning and definition pinning, hardened sandboxes at scale, isolated browser agents, delegated authorization with token exchange, multi-tenant tool servers, sagas and compensation, approval at scale, tool SLOs, usability evaluation with simulated users, evaluation-driven tool improvement, canary releases, governance, supply chain controls, incident response and audit evidence, ending with a governed enterprise tool platform capstone.
prerequisites: Completed the Tool Calling intermediate level or operates agent tools in production with OAuth, sandboxes, approvals and tracing
Writes production Python or Go and is comfortable with Kubernetes or another container platform, PostgreSQL and Prometheus or Grafana
Has access to a Linux host or cluster for microVM or gVisor sandboxes, an OAuth server that supports token exchange such as Keycloak, and an S3-compatible object store
outcomes: Design and run a tool platform with a gateway, registry, policy as code, taint tracking and pinned tool definitions
Isolate code, browser and tenant workloads and delegate user authority to tools without confused-deputy risk
Keep multi-step actions correct and reviewable with sagas, auto-approval rules, SLOs and canary releases
Govern toolsets with inventories, supply chain controls, evaluation-driven improvement, incident response and tamper-evident audit evidence
